analytical_models.equation_role: Predict the yield strength of the recrystallised austenite matrix
analytical_models.model_note: σ_y,Rx-aust = σ0 + k_HP · d^(−1/2); applied to the B2-free 28Mn0Ni matrix, giving ~460–500 MPa.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: average recrystallised grain size in the range ~5–7 μm as in the present LDS alloys
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: σ0 and k_HP taken from Etienne et al. [33] for Fe-28.8Mn-9.4Al-0.92C (σ0 = 288 MPa, k_HP = 461 MPa μm^(1/2))
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Estimated yield strength of the recrystallised austenite is ~460–500 MPa, about 170–200 MPa less than the experimentally observed yield strength of the 28Mn0Ni alloy (670 MPa).

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In 28Mn0Ni deformed to ε~0.15, closely spaced parallel slip bands are traversed by a single dark diagonal band, consistent with slip band–annealing twin interaction (Fig. 8b).

interfaces.interface_notes: 28Mn0Ni is the B2-free reference alloy; the relevant interfaces are γ/γ grain boundaries and annealing {twin} boundaries. No γ/B2 interfaces or B2 cracking occur in this grade.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation glide in the γ-matrix; isolated dislocation pinning at low strain (~0.015); dynamic slip band refinement at higher strain with homogeneous slip band spacing of ~100–200 nm at ε~0.15. Slip bands interact with annealing twin boundaries. As the alloy is B2-free, no γ/B2 interface slip-transfer behaviour applies.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: 28Mn0Ni (B2-free) is the reference alloy vs B2-containing 15Mn5Ni: lower macro-hardness (difference ~HV120) and lower yield strength (difference ~450 MPa) but far higher ductility (68% vs 20% elongation); 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni have nearly similar properties (55–68% elongation)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The three austenitic LDS grades (28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni, 15Mn5Ni) were prepared by the vacuum induction melting route; 30 kg ingots were produced.
Defect-free portions of the ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours (parent process proc_homogenised-1423k).
Hot rolling of the homogenised ingots was carried out at 1323 K; total thickness reduction of nearly 85% with ~15% reduction per pass. Same schedule applied to all three LDS grades.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: ~85% total thickness reduction, ~15% reduction per pass

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled 28Mn0Ni (Ni-free, B2-free LDS) consists primarily of a single-phase equiaxed austenite (γ) matrix containing fine κ-carbide ((FeMn)3AlC) precipitates. The optical microstructure (Fig. 1a,b) shows equiaxed grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles, essentially single phase, very distinct from the two-phase Ni-containing grades.

unmapped_findings: 28Mn0Ni is the Ni-free, B2-free reference grade of the study; its hot-rolled microstructure is essentially single-phase austenite with fine κ-carbides, unlike the two-phase B2-containing 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni grades (Table 1 composition: Mn 28.3, Al 9.0, C 0.9, Ni –, Fe balance).

The differences in hardness and yield strength between the B2-free 28Mn0Ni and B2-containing 15Mn5Ni are about HV120 and 450 MPa, respectively; 15Mn5Ni exhibited only ~20% total elongation versus 55–68% for the 28Mn(0,5)Ni alloys.
Strain hardening exponent n at higher tensile strains is ~0.30 for 28Mn0Ni (same as 28Mn5Ni) and ~0.16 for 15Mn5Ni; no plateau was observed in the stress–strain curves.

Localised nanoindentation (γ-matrix vs B2) was reported only for the 15Mn5Ni alloy (γ: 6.7 ± 0.5 GPa, B2: 6.8 ± 0.3 GPa with pop-in events); no nanoindentation hardness values for 28Mn0Ni are reported, so the nanoindentation hardness column for 28Mn0Ni in Table 3 is '-'.
